title: Proc-Macro Boundaries

writing.exampleCaption: The example makes the contract visible in code.
writing.explanation:
A procedural macro is compiled for and runs on the build host, then emits tokens for the target crate. It cannot depend on target runtime state and should emit spans that point errors back to useful input.

Procedural macros run as host tools during compilation. They receive token input from the crate being built and return token output that the compiler later checks for the target. If you cross-compile from a Mac to a phone, the macro runs on the Mac; generated program code targets the phone. This is why host dependencies and target dependencies can have different requirements, and why a restricted on-device compiler may not support arbitrary proc-macro crates. Keep the generated program independent of accidental host-only paths or environment details.

Good diagnostics are part of the macro's public API. A derive that rejects an unsupported enum should point to the enum or offending field rather than failing with a cryptic token-stream panic. Parse input using an appropriate syntax library when available, preserve useful spans, and add compile-fail examples for invalid forms. Avoid doing network or filesystem work at expansion time unless the build contract explicitly depends on it; such hidden inputs make builds difficult to reproduce. Test the macro in a separate consumer crate, including renamed dependencies and generic types. If a small trait implementation is clearer without generation, prefer it. A proc macro should remove mechanical repetition while making the generated contract easier, not harder, to audit.

A procedural macro is code executed during the build, so dependency updates to that crate deserve the same review as other build tooling. Pin versions where reproducibility matters and avoid hidden environment-dependent output. If the macro emits code with an unexpected import, prefer absolute paths or documented helper crates. The generated API should still be understandable without reading the macro implementation.
